details.description: Qwen3-Reranker-8B is a text reranking (cross-encoder) model from Alibaba's Qwen team, the largest of three sizes (0.6B, 4B, 8B) in the Qwen3 Embedding series, built on the Qwen3-8B-Base language model. It scores query-document pairs for relevance so a search or retrieval pipeline can re-rank candidates from a first-stage retriever. It supports over 100 languages, including programming languages, and accepts custom, task-specific instructions.
advantages: Qwen reports a CMTEB-R score of 77.45 for this model, the highest among the three Qwen3-Reranker sizes on that benchmark.
Qwen reports an MMTEB-R score of 72.94 and an MLDR score of 70.19, both its best results among the three Qwen3-Reranker sizes.

Qwen reports an MTEB-Code score of 81.22, ahead of the comparison rerankers Jina-multilingual-reranker-v2-base (58.98), gte-multilingual-reranker-base (54.18) and BGE-reranker-v2-m3 (41.38) in the same evaluation table.
Supports over 100 languages, including programming languages, per the Qwen3-Reranker model card.
disadvantages: Largest and presumably slowest and most resource-intensive model in the Qwen3-Reranker family; Qwen's own evaluation table shows the smaller 4B variant scores higher on MTEB-R.
use_cases: Re-ranking candidate passages retrieved by a first-stage retriever for web or document search

notes: Qwen's model card states a 32K context length, but Fireworks' host page and the catalog's own facts both give 40960 (40.9k) tokens for this deployment; kept the catalog's figure per instructions and note the model card's smaller number here. Languages are stated only as a count ('100+ languages'), so the languages list is left empty. FollowIR scores appear in Qwen's evaluation table (8.05 for this model) but were left out of evaluations since it is a p-MRR metric that can go negative for other models in the same table, not a bounded accuracy-style score. No deprecation or legacy notice found for this model.
